pr_title: http2: add support for sensitive headers
pr_body:

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/34091

pr_comments: Fwiw, if we do decide that we need more granularity for multi-value headers like `set-cookie`, I would suggest allowing the property to be a function `({ key, value }) => boolean` instead of an Array, to give the user full control. But as mentioned in the issue, I suspect that’s rare enough that we might not need to implement that?

Nice work! 

Just in case you find some issue testing, it appears as though all `'Authorization'` and `cookie` headers under 20-length appear to be forced as not-indexed via `nghttp2`

https://github.com/nghttp2/nghttp2/blob/5ae9bb8925c1cb1e945b41d140367f27b3dd5c98/lib/nghttp2_hd.c#L1358-L1367 

So, if you see `cookie` always being `not-index` despite never setting it on NodeJS, that might why.
@clshortfuse Thanks, that’s very good to know – because the test just tested this for `cookie`. I’ve updated this a bit, please take a look. :)

![wireshark-never-indexed](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9271155/86271584-272ff200-bb9b-11ea-8e5e-c90b34bee911.png)

Confirmed via Wireshark that it works! Nice job @addaleax
This does not land cleanly on v14.x since it touches files related to the QUIC implementation. Should this be backported?

A note here: this is marked as a semver-minor change, but I think it's actually a breaking change (and because of that, I don't think it should be backported to v14!). Certainly it breaks my application, and may well break things for anybody else who iterates over `request.headers`. Specifically:

* Before this change, keys in incoming HTTP headers were always strings - now one is a symbol (I currently use `headerName.startsWith(':')` to look for psuedoheaders, and my code now crashes because you can't do that with symbols).
* Before this change, every key in the headers object represented a received header, and could be interpreted as such, whilst now some keys are instead in-band special values. That matters because it might not be correct to forward this value when proxying requests, it is definitely not correctly to forward this value when translating HTTP/2 requests to HTTP/1, and it probably shouldn't be treated as a header when validating incoming headers, in metrics & logging contexts, etc etc etc.

Ofc this is a manageable breaking change, and I can still see arguments for doing this in-band rather than as a separate option, but it is going to break things and it should be advertised as such imo.

@pimterry How are you iterating through keys? I've just checked and Symbols don't appear in 

* `Object.keys(obj)`
* `for (var key in obj) `
* `Object.entries(obj)`
* `Object.getOwnPropertyNames(obj)`

Edit: TIL `Reflect.ownKeys(obj)` will.

issue_context.title: http2: support adding never-index header fields
issue_context.body:
As part of the HTTP2 (and HTTP3) spec, some headers can be sent as `Literal Header Field Never Indexed`
 
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7541.html#section-6.2.3

This can be used for security reasons to avoid `CRIME` (Compression Ratio Info-leak Made Easy) attacks to expose sensitive information. 

Points of interest are:

* [What flag to set for nghttp2](https://nghttp2.org/documentation/enums.html#c.NGHTTP2_NV_FLAG_NO_INDEX)
* [How we compile a header from JS](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/241ed44a0b06db45c97681c164fc1098e7c9f0d2/lib/internal/http2/util.js#L439)
* [How we submit responses to nghttp2](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/f63436d190b60e12131036aa9d1888d9023e9127/src/node_http2.cc#L2001)

It'll help diagnose https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/28632
comments:
This is definitely something that was considered early on when I did the initial implementation. It is hampered by the fact that we tried to keep the API for headers in http/2 as close as possible to that of http/1, which uses a simple object to express headers... e.g.

```js
{
  ":method": "GET",
  "content-type": "text/plain",
  "abc": ["value 1", "value 2"]
}
```

The difficulty here becomes: how do we indicate which headers should not be indexed? Should it be specified per-request? Should it be specified separately from the actual header pairs?

One way we could do this could be to allow a list of never-index header names as options whenever headers are specified... e.g.

```js
stream.respond({
  'content-type': 'text/plain',
  'abc': ['value 1', 'value 2']
}, { neverIndex: ['abc'] });
```

Each method that accepts headers would need to be updated to accept an options object. This seems like the most ergonomic way to go.
@jasnell Just for context, I am already working on this :)

Fwiw, I’m taking the Symbol-based approach (because I think information about headers should be passed in the headers object), but I’m not sure if we really want this kind of subdivision – if one of the cookie headers is sensitive, it’s probably okay to mark the others as sensitive as well.

review_comments: It’s intentional – I’ll add a comment :+1:
